title: Throttle Position Output Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the throttle position output circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. The engine computer shares the throttle position with other modules over this line.
symptoms: Possible shifting, idle or gauge problems on systems that use the signal

causes.name: Wiring or connector fault between the engine computer and the module receiving the signal
Corroded or loose connector
Fault in the receiving module
Engine computer output fault

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the throttle position output circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the wiring or connector; module replacement is only needed if the circuit tests good.

title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the injection control pressure regulator circuit and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. On some diesels this valve sets the high oil pressure used to fire the fuel injectors.

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the injection control pressure regulator (IPR) valve
Broken or chafed wire in the injection control pressure regulator circuit
Failed injection control pressure regulator (IPR) valve
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the injection control pressure regulator circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the injection control pressure regulator (IPR) valve.

title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the injection control pressure regulator circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. On some diesels this valve sets the high oil pressure used to fire the fuel injectors.

causes.name: Control wire to the injection control pressure regulator (IPR) valve shorted to ground
Failed injection control pressure regulator (IPR) valve
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the injection control pressure regulator circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the injection control pressure regulator (IPR) valve.

title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The computer is watching the O2 sensor pumping current trim circuit (bank 1 sensor 1) and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. This is a calibration circuit inside the front wide-range (air-fuel ratio) oxygen sensor.
symptoms: Possible rough running or lower fuel economy

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the front wide-range oxygen sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the O2 sensor pumping current trim circuit (bank 1 sensor 1)
Failed front wide-range oxygen sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the O2 sensor pumping current trim circuit (bank 1 sensor 1), checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the front wide-range oxygen sensor.

Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the front wide-range oxygen sensor.

title: Fuel Pump "B" Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the fuel pump "B" control circuit and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. Some vehicles have a second fuel pump, or a pump run by its own control module.

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the secondary fuel pump or its driver module
Broken or chafed wire in the fuel pump "B" control circuit
Failed secondary fuel pump or its driver module
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the fuel pump "B" control circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the secondary fuel pump or its driver module.

title: Fuel Pump "A" Low Flow/Performance
plain: The main fuel pump is not delivering as much fuel or pressure as the engine computer expects.
symptoms: Hesitation or loss of power, especially under load

causes.name: Weak or worn fuel pump
Clogged fuel filter or pump strainer
Poor connection or voltage drop at the pump
Faulty fuel pump driver module or relay
Faulty fuel pressure sensor

checks: Measure fuel pressure and compare it with the maker spec
Check voltage and ground at the fuel pump connector
Replace the fuel filter if it is serviceable
fix: Usually a new fuel pump assembly, after confirming good voltage and a clean filter.

title: Fuel Pump "B" Low Flow/Performance
plain: The second fuel pump (on vehicles that have one) is not delivering the fuel flow or pressure the computer expects.

causes.name: Weak secondary fuel pump
Clogged filter or strainer
Wiring or voltage drop at the pump
Faulty fuel pump driver module

checks: Measure fuel pressure and flow
Check voltage and ground at the pump
fix: Replace the weak pump or clogged filter after checking the wiring.

title: Torque Management Feedback Signal "A"
plain: The computer is watching the torque management feedback signal and has spotted a fault in its circuit. The engine computer uses this signal to report back to other modules (often the transmission) how much torque it is making.

causes.name: Wiring or connector fault between the engine and transmission computers
Network communication problem between modules
Module software that needs an update
Engine or transmission computer fault

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the torque management feedback signal, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or network fault, or update the module software as the maker directs.

title: Torque Management Feedback Signal "A" Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the torque management feedback signal and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. The engine computer uses this signal to report back to other modules (often the transmission) how much torque it is making.

causes.name: Wiring or connector fault between the engine and transmission computers
Network communication problem between modules
Module software that needs an update
Engine or transmission computer fault

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the torque management feedback signal reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Repair the wiring or network fault, or update the module software as the maker directs.

title: "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1)
plain: The computer is watching the "A" rocker arm actuator control circuit (bank 1) and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. This oil-operated part switches the valves between low and high lift, like Honda VTEC.
symptoms: Loss of power, especially at higher rpm
Rough idle or hesitation in some cases

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the rocker arm oil control solenoid
Broken or chafed wire in the "A" rocker arm actuator control circuit (bank 1)
Failed rocker arm oil control solenoid
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the "A" rocker arm actuator control circuit (bank 1), checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the rocker arm oil control solenoid.

title: "A" Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off (Bank 1)
plain: The variable valve lift system (like Honda VTEC) is not switching on when the computer asks, often because of low or dirty oil.
symptoms: Loss of power at higher rpm
Engine may feel flat above mid-range

causes.name: Engine oil low, dirty or the wrong thickness
Clogged screen or filter at the rocker arm (VTEC) solenoid
Faulty rocker arm oil pressure switch
Sticking rocker arm oil control solenoid
Wiring fault at the solenoid or pressure switch

checks: Check the oil level and change the oil if it is old or the wrong type
Remove and clean the screen at the solenoid
Check the oil pressure switch and solenoid operation with a scan tool
fix: Often fixed with fresh oil of the right type and a clean solenoid screen; otherwise replace the oil pressure switch or solenoid.

cost.job: Replace VTEC oil pressure switch or solenoid

examples: Common on Honda Accord, Civic and CR-V engines with VTEC, often when oil is low or overdue

title: "A" Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On (Bank 1)
plain: The variable valve lift system (like Honda VTEC) seems to stay switched on when it should be off.

causes.name: Faulty rocker arm oil pressure switch
Sticking rocker arm oil control solenoid
Dirty or sludgy engine oil
Wrong oil thickness
Wiring short in the pressure switch circuit

checks: Check the oil level and condition
Watch the oil pressure switch reading with the engine idling
Unplug the solenoid and see if the switch reading changes
fix: Most often a new oil pressure switch or solenoid, plus an oil change if the oil is dirty.

cost.job: Replace VTEC oil pressure switch or solenoid

examples: Seen on Honda and Acura engines with VTEC

title: "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit (Bank 1)
plain: The computer is watching the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1) and has spotted a fault in its circuit. This sensor tells the computer which valve lift mode the rocker arms are actually in.
symptoms: Variable valve lift may be disabled
Possible loss of power at higher rpm

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the rocker arm actuator position sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1) circuit
Failed rocker arm actuator position sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1), checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the rocker arm actuator position sensor.

title: "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
plain: The computer is watching the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1) and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. This sensor tells the computer which valve lift mode the rocker arms are actually in.

Possible loss of power at higher rpm

causes.name: Failing or sticking rocker arm actuator position sensor
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1) reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the rocker arm actuator position sensor itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.
